claim.pdf_says: In the 'where program-prototype is:' and 'where function-prototype is:' skeletons the required words are underlined and the optional word IS is NOT: 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.' (both underlined), 'PROGRAM-ID.' / 'FUNCTION-ID.' (underlined), 'AS' (underlined), 'IS' (NOT underlined), 'PROTOTYPE.' (underlined), 'END PROGRAM' / 'END FUNCTION' (both words underlined). Verified at 300 dpi.
claim.markdown_says:
[ IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. ]

PROGRAM-ID. program-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] IS PROTOTYPE.

[ options-paragraph ]
… (identically for FUNCTION-ID. / END FUNCTION) — plain text, no underline markup and no 'Figure notes' paragraph recording which words are underlined.
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2 an underlined word is required and a non-underlined reserved word is an optional word that may be omitted. The transcription drops the distinction entirely for these two skeletons, so 'IS' reads as mandatory when 'PROGRAM-ID. name PROTOTYPE.' is legal source — exactly the falsely-restrictive-syntax failure mode. Every other figure on these pages carries a Figure-notes paragraph recording underlining; these two do not.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED as a genuine content loss, but the claim's supporting rationale is partly wrong and its severity is overstated.

(1) The PDF reading is exactly right, and I confirmed it forensically rather than by eye. Rendering page 286 at 300 dpi and measuring dark-pixel coverage on the underline row (y=1493) of the program-prototype PROGRAM-ID line gives: PROGRAM-ID. 259/300 px = 86.3%, AS 41/60 px = 68.3%, PROTOTYPE. 240/250 px = 96.0%, and IS 0/70 px = 0.0%. Zero ink under IS on the row where the neighbouring words carry a solid rule. The same layout repeats on the FUNCTION-ID line (solid underline row at y=2250-2251). At 2x upscaling the gap is visible directly: the short rule under AS stops, IS sits on clean white, then the long rule under PROTOTYPE. begins. IDENTIFICATION and DIVISION. are separately underlined, and END + PROGRAM / END + FUNCTION are each underlined. Every particular of the claimed PDF reading holds.

(2) The markdown reading is also right. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines ~12455-12490 render both skeletons as bare plain text — no <u> markup, no Figure-notes paragraph. The transcription demonstrably owns a convention for this (97 <u> tags and 225 'Figure notes' paragraphs document-wide), and it applied that convention to the immediately adjacent sibling figure: the page-287 program-definition skeleton carries a Figure-notes paragraph ending 'Underlined (required) words in the printed figure: IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, PROGRAM-ID, AS, COMMON, INITIAL, RECURSIVE, END, PROGRAM.' — pointedly omitting IS. So the two page-286 skeletons are an inconsistent application of the transcription's own mechanism, and a reader working from §10.6.1 alone concludes IS is required when it is not. Underlining in a COBOL general format is not decoration: 5.2.6.2 makes it the standard's metalanguage for required-vs-optional, as load-bearing as a bracket pair. This is therefore a content difference, not the formatting/line-wrapping/page-furniture class of non-finding.

(3) CORRECTION to the claim's rationale. 'Every other figure on these pages carries a Figure-notes paragraph recording underlining; these two do not' is FALSE. The page-287 function-definition skeleton and the page-288 class-definition, factory-definition and instance-definition skeletons carry neither figure notes nor underline markup. Dropping underlines in the §10.6 'where X is:' skeletons is the norm across this run of pages; only the program-definition figure got the note, and it got it because of the choice-indicator hazard, not the underlining.

(4) CORRECTION to severity. The distinction is NOT lost from the document. The transcription already encodes it correctly in both normative clause-level general formats: §11.5.2 Format 2 (prototype) reads '<u>FUNCTION-ID</u>. function-prototype-name-1 [ <u>AS</u> literal-1 ] IS <u>PROTOTYPE</u>.' and §11.10.2 Format 2 (prototype) reads '<u>PROGRAM-ID</u>. program-prototype-name-1 [ <u>AS</u> literal-1 ] IS <u>PROTOTYPE</u> .' — both leaving IS unmarked, i.e. optional, matching the PDF. Nowhere does the transcription assert that IS is mandatory, and an implementer deriving the PROGRAM-ID / FUNCTION-ID paragraph syntax goes to §11.5 / §11.10, which are correct. §10.6.1 is a structural overview restatement of formats specified normatively elsewhere. The real-world falsely-restrictive-parser risk is therefore low.

Net: real, because a normative 5.2.6.2 distinction printed in the PDF is absent from a figure the transcription itself headings 'General format', and the page read in isolation yields a wrong answer about legal source. But it is a fidelity gap in a duplicated overview figure with a correct authoritative twin two clauses away — minor-to-moderate, not structural.
verdict.corrected_description: Page 286, §10.6.1: in the 'where program-prototype is:' and 'where function-prototype is:' skeletons the PDF prints underlines that per 5.2.6.2 mark required words — IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION., PROGRAM-ID. / FUNCTION-ID., AS, PROTOTYPE., END, PROGRAM / FUNCTION — and pointedly leaves IS un-underlined (forensically 0% ink coverage on the underline row vs 68-96% for its neighbours), making 'PROGRAM-ID. name PROTOTYPE.' legal. The markdown transcribes both skeletons as plain text with no <u> markup and no Figure-notes paragraph, so the required/optional distinction is absent from the page. Two corrections to the original claim: (a) it is NOT the case that every other figure on these pages carries a Figure-notes paragraph — the page-287 function-definition and the page-288 class-, factory- and instance-definition skeletons are equally unannotated, so these two are not anomalous on this run of pages; (b) severity is overstated as 'structural' — the transcription already records the distinction correctly in the normative general formats at §11.5.2 Format 2 and §11.10.2 Format 2, both of which leave IS unmarked, so the document never asserts IS is mandatory and an implementer working from the authoritative clause gets the right answer. Suggested fix: add a Figure-notes paragraph to the two page-286 skeletons naming the underlined words and stating that IS is an optional word, matching the treatment already given to the page-287 program-definition figure.

evidence.refuted_sub_claim: 'Every other figure on these pages carries a Figure-notes paragraph' — false; pages 287 (function-definition) and 288 (class-, factory-, instance-definition) carry none.
